triage.expected: Images stay on the same line as the surrounding text.
triage.actual: Each image renders on its own line; the header text is pushed out of view.

repro.location: Web app > channel header > inline Markdown images
repro.trigger: Header text with two inline images, after the images load
repro.expected: Images and text on one row
repro.observed: Each image on its own row (computed display: block)
repro.pattern: Every inline Markdown image once loaded: channel header, header-change system message, messages with several images. Images still loading are not affected.

repro.repro_script:
"""Repro: inline Markdown images in the channel header wrap onto their own lines. Exit 1 = bug present."""
import sys
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

with sync_playwright() as p:
    page = p.chromium.launch().new_page()
    page.goto(f"{BASE}/{TEAM}/channels/{CHANNEL}")  # placeholders set by the sandbox
    page.wait_for_selector(".channel-header__description .file-preview__button img")
    tops = page.eval_on_selector_all(
        ".channel-header__description .file-preview__button",
        "els => els.map(e => [getComputedStyle(e).display, e.getBoundingClientRect().top])")
    # Two images and the text should share one row; display:block stacks them.
    sys.exit(1 if any(d == "block" for d, _ in tops) or len({round(t) for _, t in tops}) > 1 else 0)

diagnosis.summary: Inline Markdown images lose their place in the line of text, and each one wraps onto its own line.

suspects.explanation: Once the image loads, SizeAwareImage sets display: block as an inline style on .file-preview__button. Inline styles beat stylesheets, so the inline-block rules never apply.
suspects.evidence: The element's style attribute reads display: block after load.

lines: width: this.state.imageWidth + 2, // 2px to account for the border

caveats: SizeAwareImage is shared by attachments and MM Blocks; their block layout depends on the stylesheet once the inline style is gone.

winning_fix.notes: Repro exits 0 with the patch; existing web app tests pass.
